title: Investigate CPU/NUMA pinning impact and document when it applies (host-level tuning)
creator: Noah Patel
project: Hardware tuning profiles pack (Serving Runtime Performance — Kernel + Scheduling)
description:
Context
- As part of the hardware tuning profiles pack, we need a clear stance on host-level recommendations we can safely document and (where possible) enforce.
- CPU pinning / NUMA placement has come up repeatedly in perf investigations (tail latency variance, jitter under mixed workloads), but applicability depends heavily on deployment mode (Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private), topology (single vs dual socket), and GPU interconnect (PCIe vs SXM).

Goal
- Quantify whether CPU pinning / NUMA placement provides measurable benefit (p95/p99 latency, jitter, throughput stability) for Redwood runtime.
- Produce actionable guidance: when we recommend it, when we require it (if ever), and when it’s not worth the operational complexity.
- Ensure guidance cleanly maps to what we control:
  - Hosted: limited/indirect control (K8s topology manager, cpusets, node pools)
  - Dedicated: moderate control (we control fleet images and node config)
  - Private: variable (customer-owned environments; docs + installer warnings)

Scope
- Evaluate CPU pinning for:
  - runtime main process threads (scheduler, tokenization, networking)
  - per-request CPU workers (if any) and background tasks (metrics export)
- Evaluate NUMA placement for:
  - dual-socket hosts where GPUs are attached to a specific NUMA node
  - PCIe GPUs (notably L40S) where cross-socket traffic is more common
- Keep it pragmatic: results should translate into a small set of recommended knobs / best practices (not a 20-step tuning guide).

Benchmark setup (what we ran)
- Hardware
  - L40S PCIe (dual socket) pool used by benchmark-lab
  - H100 SXM (single socket) pool used by benchmark-lab
- Workload buckets (aligned to profile pack buckets)
  - Short prefill / short decode (chatty)
  - Long prefill / short decode (RAG-ish)
  - Long prefill / long decode (batchy, high GPU residency)
  - Mixed bucket (weighted mix; induces queueing variance)
- Metrics
  - end-to-end latency p50/p95/p99
  - scheduler_queue_ms (if enabled)
  - tokens/sec aggregate and per-GPU
  - CPU util per socket, run queue length, context switches (host)

Interventions tested
1) Baseline: no explicit pinning (default OS scheduler / K8s)
2) CPU pinning only: pin runtime process to a dedicated CPU set (avoid sharing with kubelet/system)
3) CPU + NUMA alignment: pin runtime CPUs to the NUMA node local to the primary GPU(s), and avoid cross-socket IRQ affinity drift

Summary of findings
- L40S (dual-socket PCIe)
  - CPU + NUMA alignment reduced tail jitter in mixed workloads.
  - Observed improvements were most consistent in p99 latency and variance, not raw throughput.
  - Representative deltas (mixed bucket, steady-state):
    - p99 latency: 4–9% improvement vs baseline (most runs clustered ~6%)
    - p95 latency: 1–4% improvement
    - tokens/sec: within noise (±1–2%)
  - When we did NOT see benefit:
    - purely GPU-bound long decode with high batch (CPU overhead amortized)
  - When it helped most:
    - mixed workloads where scheduler_queue_ms had spikes; pinning reduced queue jitter correlated with cross-socket migrations.

- H100 (SXM; benchmark hosts were effectively single-socket / well-balanced)
  - Improvements were small and inconsistent.
  - Representative deltas (mixed bucket):
    - p99 latency: 0–3% (often within run-to-run noise)
    - throughput: no meaningful change
  - Main conclusion: for our current H100 Hosted/Dedicated fleet configuration, CPU pinning is best-effort only; not worth making a “required” step.

Operational guidance (what we will document)
- Hosted
  - Best-effort only. We should not document CPU/NUMA pinning as a user-facing requirement.
  - Action: ensure our node pools / daemonset configs keep topology manager enabled where available and avoid CPU contention from system pods.

- Dedicated
  - Recommended for L40S PCIe dual-socket nodes.
  - Optional for H100 (no strong evidence it helps enough to justify complexity).
  - Practical guidance: reserve a CPU set for runtime, keep it local to the GPU NUMA node, and keep system services off those cores.

- Private
  - Recommended when customers run:
    - L40S (or similar PCIe GPUs) on dual-socket hosts, OR
    - any configuration where GPUs are not uniformly distributed across sockets and CPU migrations are frequent.
  - Not required for correctness, but can reduce tail latency variance.
  - We should include a short “decision tree” in docs + installer warnings:
    - If dual-socket + PCIe GPU → recommend NUMA alignment
    - If single-socket or SXM/NVLink-balanced topology → no action needed

What’s NOT going into the profile pack
- No new profile knobs that silently assume CPU pinning.
- No requirement gates that block profile selection based on CPU pinning being present (too hard to validate reliably across deployment modes).

Deliverables from this ticket
- Documented guidance for when CPU/NUMA pinning applies (to be referenced by profile pack overview + Private installer docs).
- Concrete recommendation text + minimal commands/examples for Dedicated/Private.

Links / artifacts
- Benchmark notes: Google Drive scratchpad: working-notes-kernel-vs-scheduler-knobs (section: “Host-level tuning: CPU/NUMA pinning”)
- Benchmark-lab runs tagged: profilepack.hosttuning.numa.v1 (see benchmark-lab dashboard; ask Rina Kobayashi for direct link)
- Related docs to update:
  - Confluence: hardware-tuning-profiles-pack-overview
  - Confluence: hardware-sku-constraints-for-profiles (add topology assumptions for L40S nodes)

Open questions / follow-ups
- Do we want to ship a small helper in Private installer to print detected NUMA topology and recommended cpuset ranges?
- Should we standardize IRQ affinity on L40S nodes in Dedicated fleet image, or keep it as a troubleshooting-only tool?
acceptance_criteria:
1) Run benchmark-lab comparison for L40S and H100 with/without CPU pinning and NUMA alignment on the mixed bucket.
2) Summarize p95/p99 impact and whether results are consistent enough to recommend.
3) Provide clear guidance by deployment mode (Hosted/Dedicated/Private) and topology (single vs dual socket).
4) Identify any required infra changes vs “best-effort” documentation-only recommendations.
outcome: CPU/NUMA pinning meaningfully reduces tail latency variance on dual-socket L40S PCIe nodes (p99 improved ~4–9% in mixed workloads). On H100 SXM nodes in our current fleet configuration, benefit is small/inconsistent (0–3% p99). Guidance will be documented as recommended for Dedicated/Private on dual-socket PCIe GPU hosts, best-effort only for Hosted, and optional for H100.

comments: 2026-01-20 (Irene Choi): Pulled 2x L40S dual-socket nodes in benchmark-lab. Baseline runs show noticeable p99 jitter in mixed bucket (scheduler_queue_ms spikes). Will rerun with cpuset + NUMA bind.
2026-01-27 (Marcus Reed): Added host telemetry capture (run queue, context switches) to the run template. Seeing cross-socket migrations correlate with latency spikes on L40S baseline.

2026-02-02 (Irene Choi): Results: L40S mixed bucket p99 improved ~6% median across 5 runs with CPU+NUMA alignment; throughput flat. H100 results within noise; no clear win. Proposing: recommend for L40S dual-socket Dedicated/Private only.
2026-02-06 (Sean Gallagher): From SRE perspective: please keep this as recommendation not rollout gate. We can’t reliably detect pinning correctness in Hosted, and false positives would be painful.
2026-02-12 (Noah Patel): Agree. Let’s document a decision tree and keep profiles independent of host tuning. If we want stronger enforcement later, it should be in fleet image config, not runtime.

2026-02-21 (Irene Choi): Drafted doc text and sent to Elliot Price + Kira Thompson for doc integration. Marking ticket Done; will track any installer helper as separate follow-up if we choose to build it.
